title: How do four number names become numbers?
description: Four number names, two in the Indian system and two in the American system, are changed into digits group by group, with zeros in the empty places. The American ones are cut again into Indian groups, and each answer is read back to check.
teaching_notes: One idea: every group keeps its own count of digits, so an empty place is filled with zeros before the commas are placed in the Indian way. Ask the class how many digits the lakh group holds before any name is written. Watch for students who keep the American threes when the Indian form is asked for.

source: Figure it Out, Q2 (names to numerals)
video_script.why: The child has placed commas in both systems and read a ten digit number, and now goes the other way, from names to numbers.
video_script.substitution: Write each group of the name with its own count of digits, fill empty places with zeros, join the groups, and cut the Indian way.
video_script.anchor: Four number names written out in words, with a row of Indian groups and a row of American groups under them.
video_script.payoff_line: Each name is now written as a number with Indian commas

final_answer.spoken: one crore one lakh one thousand ten, one arab ten lakh one thousand one, ten crore twenty lakh thirty thousand forty, and nine arab eight crore seven lakh six hundred

never_show: a comma written answer before the answer beat
maths_rules: one crore one lakh one thousand ten: groups 1 | 01 | 01 | 010, digits 10101010, Indian form 1,01,01,010
one billion one million one thousand one: American groups 1 | 001 | 001 | 001, digits 1001001001, Indian cut 1 | 00 | 10 | 01 | 001, Indian form 1,00,10,01,001
ten crore twenty lakh thirty thousand forty: groups 10 | 20 | 30 | 040, digits 102030040, Indian form 10,20,30,040
nine billion eighty million seven hundred thousand six hundred: American groups 9 | 080 | 700 | 600, digits 9080700600, Indian cut 9 | 08 | 07 | 00 | 600, Indian form 9,08,07,00,600
check: 1 arab 10 lakh 1 thousand 1 = 1 billion 1 million 1 thousand 1, since 1 arab = 1 billion and 10 lakh = 1 million
check: 9 arab 8 crore 7 lakh 600 = 9 billion 80 million 700 thousand 600, since 8 crore = 80 million and 7 lakh = 700 thousand
digit counts of the answers are 8, 10, 9 and 10

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Every group of a number keeps its own count of digits.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>In the Indian system the last group has three digits. The thousand, lakh and crore groups have two each.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>In the American system every group has three digits. An empty place is filled with zeros. We work the same way as the example in your book.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, the first name is one crore, one lakh, one thousand and ten. The lakh group needs two digits, so one lakh is zero one.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The thousand group is zero one, and ten in the last group is zero one zero.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The groups are one, zero one, zero one and zero one zero.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>The third name is ten crore, twenty lakh, thirty thousand and forty. Its groups are ten, twenty, thirty and zero four zero.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: one billion one million one thousand one = American 1 | 001 | 001 | 001, digits 1001001001; Indian cut 1 | 00 | 10 | 01 | 001

marks.m1: the second name is written in American boxes
marks.m3: the ten digits are cut again as 1 | 00 | 10 | 01 | 001

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, the second name is one billion, one million, one thousand and one. In the American system every group has three digits.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The groups are one, zero zero one, zero zero one and zero zero one. Joined, they make one zero zero one zero zero one zero zero one.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Cut it the Indian way, three digits from the right and then twos. The groups are one, zero zero, one zero, zero one and zero zero one.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: nine billion eighty million seven hundred thousand six hundred = American 9 | 080 | 700 | 600, digits 9080700600; Indian cut 9 | 08 | 07 | 00 | 600

marks.m1: the fourth name is written in American boxes
marks.m3: the ten digits are cut again as 9 | 08 | 07 | 00 | 600

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, the fourth name is nine billion, eighty million, seven hundred thousand and six hundred.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The American groups are nine, zero eight zero, seven zero zero and six zero zero. Joined, they make nine zero eight zero seven zero zero six zero zero.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Cut the Indian way. The groups are nine, zero eight, zero seven, zero zero and six zero zero.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: check by reading back: 1 arab 10 lakh 1 thousand 1 = 1 billion 1 million 1 thousand 1; 9 arab 8 crore 7 lakh 600 = 9 billion 80 million 700 thousand 600

marks.m2: 10 lakh is matched with 1 million and 1 arab with 1 billion
marks.m3: 8 crore is matched with 80 million and 7 lakh with 700 thousand

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, check by reading each answer back in words. The first and third read back the names we were given.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The second reads one arab, ten lakh, one thousand, one. An arab is a billion and ten lakh is a million, so it matches.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The last reads nine arab, eight crore, seven lakh, six hundred. Eight crore is eighty million and seven lakh is seven hundred thousand, so it matches too.
